title: US real average hourly earnings, July 2026
question: What will the first BLS Table A-1 print show for the July 2026 seasonally adjusted over-the-month percent change in real average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls?
resolutionSource: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Real Earnings Table A-1
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first BLS Real Earnings Table A-1 value for July 2026, seasonally adjusted over-the-month percent change in real average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls, as first printed on the official release page; use the one-decimal percent value shown by BLS and do not revise for later updates.
drivers: Nominal average-hourly-earnings growth relative to CPI-U

reasoning.text: July 2026 real average hourly earnings first print

The resolver is BLS Real Earnings Table A-1: the seasonally adjusted over-the-month percent change in real average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls. Anchors and history below use this same Table A-1 all-employees, seasonally adjusted variant; this target resolves to its first printed one-decimal value, without later revision.

reasoning.call: Fetched the official BLS August 2026 release-calendar entry for the target release date.
reasoning.result: The BLS calendar lists Real Earnings for July 2026 at 08:30 AM ET on Wednesday, August 12, 2026; the calendar page was last modified June 10, 2026.

reasoning.call: Fetched the current official BLS Real Earnings Table A-1 release for the latest available May 2026 observation.
reasoning.result: May 2026 Table A-1 reports real average hourly earnings at $11.24 and an over-the-month change of -0.1 percent; April was $11.25 and -0.5 percent, while March was $11.31 and -0.6 percent.

reasoning.call: Fetched the official BLS April 2026 Real Earnings release for the March first-print Table A-1 result.
reasoning.result: The March 2026 BLS release reports that real average hourly earnings for all employees decreased 0.6 percent over the month; its Table A-1 level is $11.31.

reasoning.call: Fetched the official BLS March 2026 Real Earnings release for the February first-print Table A-1 result.
reasoning.result: The February 2026 BLS release reports a 0.2 percent increase in real average hourly earnings, from $11.38 in January to $11.40 in February; nominal average hourly earnings rose 0.4 percent and CPI-U rose 0.3 percent.

reasoning.text: The reference class is monthly, seasonally adjusted Table A-1 real hourly-earnings changes. The recent base rate is slightly negative after January through May values of 0.3, 0.2, -0.6, -0.5, and -0.1 percent, but the most recent two observations show the contraction decelerating.

Prior/update/interval: I use a zero-centered persistence prior with the five fetched Table A-1 change observations (0.3, 0.2, -0.6, -0.5, -0.1). Their mean is -0.14 and population sigma = 0.36 percentage points; 1.28*sigma = 0.46 percentage points. I update the prior to 0.1 percent because May's -0.1 followed the earlier -0.6 and -0.5 declines, while the nominal-wage-minus-CPI mechanism can return a modest positive reading. Rounding the approximately 0.46-point half-width to the publication grid gives an 80% interval of -0.4 to 0.6 percent.

Upside risk is a July nominal-pay acceleration combined with subdued CPI-U, which would land above the interval if real hourly earnings rise more than 0.6 percent. Downside risk is another inflation overshoot or unfavorable high-wage/low-wage payroll-composition shift; a sufficiently large combination would land below the interval.
